note: task-128. NOT a /variants run -- nothing here was generated by this project. These twelve are OWNER-SUPPLIED PixelLab states that already existed server-side in group e2702eb6-248d-4b6b-b8dc-fedc1290e059, downloaded whole on 2026-07-31 at ZERO credit cost. There is therefore no silhouette_target, no measured band and no per-variant keep/flag verdict of the kind archer-medieval carries -- the owner's ask WAS the verdict: 'I want all these states as archers. The knight armor ones can be a single variant but not every.' What was measured is the only gate that can reject art at this size: max content bbox across all 8 rotations against the 56px atlas cell (the gate that killed the ranged-roster family in task-085). All twelve pass. Canvas is 92x92 for every state, larger than archer-medieval's 88x88, which is why the bboxes run larger than the six looks these replace. Full colour, quantize false, per docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md's 2026-07-28 amendment.

base.note: The base is itself one of the twelve -- state 'Merle_Pathfinder', shipped as slug 'hoodedbow'. Every other state in the group is an edit of it, which is why they share a hood, a palette and a stance and read as one line of soldiers rather than twelve unrelated units.

register: Hooded, cloaked, distinctly kitted. Deliberately NOT the bows-and-leather register archer-medieval holds itself to: several of these carry firearms, an RPG launcher, shoulder cannons, a mounted turret, a cyborg energy bow and a mage staff. The owner ruled the arms-and-kit register OPEN on 2026-07-31 -- canon never banned any of it; the ban was an inference drawn from the pitch-dark premise that later got cited back as canon. See the CORRECTION note in docs/data/art/families/archer-medieval/family.json, which records the same reversal from the other side.
separation_rationale: The axis here is KIT AND HEADGEAR, not proportion. That is the point: the problem task-128 exists to fix is that eleven spearman looks and six archer looks were all the same steel-helmeted body, so silhouette variety WITHIN the archer block was never the bottleneck -- the archer block reading as a different KIND OF SOLDIER from the spearman block was. Every one of these twelve differs from a spearman at the head (hood, mask, ghillie, domed helm, bare hair) before any weapon is resolved, which is the part that survives a 56px cell in a near-black frame.

naming.note: The PixelLab state folder names under RawArt/Renders/pathfinder-line/raw/ are TRUNCATED PROMPT FRAGMENTS, not names -- 'Can_we_have_one_cove', 'Lets_so_secret_servi'. They are kept on disk verbatim because that is what the retention rule preserves and what source.json's state_ids key on, but nothing ships under them. Each got a descriptive slug based on what the sprite actually looks like, in the same register as archer-medieval's v1_narrowstrung / v2_bowextended. The shipped atlas prefix is 'archer-<slug>'. 'Merle (Pathfinder)' is a LEFTOVER HERO NAME and is deliberately not propagated: the owner reversed the fixed-named-hero decision because attrition makes names hard to remember, so classes are identified by role only.

map.look: Hood up, cloak closed, longbow held down at one side, fletched arrows over the far shoulder. The base state, and the block's index 0.
Head-to-knee foliage ghillie cloak over the bow silhouette -- a ragged, fringed outline, the only broken-edge look in the block.
Hood up over a bone-white mask with one large hollow eye -- the highest-contrast head in the block, a bright disc where every other look is dark.
Short and broad under a hood, heavy forked beard filling the chest, a tool in each hand -- the only squat proportion in the block.
Hooded and mantled, a tall staff held vertical with a lit crystal at the top -- a vertical bar plus a bright point well above the head.
Hooded, one optic implant lit, a cyan energy bow drawn across the body -- the brightest whole-weapon silhouette in the block.
Dropped into a low crouch behind a long rifle held level -- the only crouched profile in the block, a horizontal bar low across the body.
Hooded, a launcher tube shouldered diagonally with a fat warhead clearing the head -- a thick diagonal crossing the whole silhouette.
The hooded bow look with two barrels mounted on the shoulders, one projecting each side -- the widest shoulder line in the block.
Heavy domed helm and goggles instead of a hood, twin muzzles at the shoulders, coiled cable at the hip -- the heaviest, most enclosed head.
Hooded and seated low behind a mounted turret emplacement -- a wide horizontal base under a small head, the only look with ground furniture.
No hood: black tactical suit, bare dark hair, compact carbine held two-handed at the waist -- the narrowest and darkest look in the block.

not_from_this_family.why: The one surviving knight-armored archer, carried over unchanged from task-126. It sits at table_index 1 -- between hoodedbow and ghilliecloak -- rather than at the end, so the two looks a reader is most likely to compare (the new default and the one that used to be the whole block) are adjacent in every report Swarm.TeamVariantReport prints.

measurement.gate: max content bbox across all 8 rotations, both walk frames, against the 56px atlas cell
measurement.source: measured by Scripts/art/pixelpipe.py pack while assembling RawArt/Sheets/T_Team_2bit.png, 2026-07-31 -- not re-derived by hand
measurement.result: all twelve PASS; widest are riflecrouch and turretnest at 53px and domedhelm at 53x50
measurement.correction: The task-128 brief's own table understated two of these widths -- it claimed 45 for Can_you_make_a_Turre and 45 for Replace_the_bow_with, both of which measure 53 across the full 8 rotations. Neither fails the gate, but the margin is 3px, not 11. Anything appended to this family later should be measured the same way rather than trusted from a brief.

retention: RawArt/Renders/pathfinder-line/raw/<folder>/rotations/*.png -- 96 PNGs, 8 rotations x 12 states, 92x92, retained permanently per the PixelLab-retention rule. RawArt/Renders/pathfinder-line/source.json holds the group id, the base id and the folder -> state_id map.
